hazard_level: High (CFL / Fluorescent) to Low (LED and Incandescent)
hazards: Compact Fluorescent Lamps (CFLs) contain toxic mercury vapor and phosphor powder. Broken glass poses severe cut hazards, and LEDs contain electronic driver components with lead.
safe_handling: Hold bulbs by the plastic or metal base rather than the glass tube. Store used bulbs in their original cardboard sleeves to prevent breakage.
unsafe_actions: Never throw CFL or LED bulbs into regular household garbage or standard glass recycling bins. Do not vacuum broken CFL glass, as this spreads mercury vapor into the air.
what_to_do_if_damaged: Open windows and leave the room for 15 minutes if a CFL breaks. Scoop up glass and powder using stiff cardboard, wipe the area with a damp paper towel, and seal everything in a glass jar or double plastic bag.
disposal_route: Hand over CFLs and LEDs to an authorized e-waste or hazardous lamp collection point.
recoverable_materials: Aluminum, copper, glass, rare earth phosphors (from CFLs), and circuit board metals (from LEDs).
environmental_impact: Broken CFLs release mercury that contaminates water bodies and enters the food chain, while discarded LEDs leach heavy metals into landfills.
